subject: Tiered usage credit mechanics + marketplace tranche for FintechCo private offer
messages:
From: Sarah Morgan <sarah@fintechco.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: 2028-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer question — tiered credits + marketplace tranche

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has asked for one clarified item before we move to legal: how the tiered usage credits interact with the marketplace private offer tranche. Specifically: if we commit to a 12-month spend band with credits that scale at three thresholds, and we route billing through AWS Marketplace (private offer), how are the credits applied and how does that affect the channel/reseller uplift?

High-level asks from our side:
- A short example (numbers) showing invoice path if we hit 70%, 100%, 130% of committed usage
- Clarity on whether credits are applied on the Redwood invoice or via the marketplace settlement to AWS (we need a clean path for our finance team)
- Any impact to the reseller margin/passback or list-price anchoring if we keep the private offer on Marketplace

Can your team sketch a worked example? We also attached the commitment worksheet for reference.

Appreciate it — Sarah
[attachment: FintechCo_PrivateOffer_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Morgan <sarah@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@fintechco.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — tiered credits + marketplace tranche

Hi Sarah — thanks for this, good question.

Short answer: credits can be modeled two ways; the best path for clean customer accounting is to keep the economic credit on Redwood's side (i.e., Redwood issues an invoice credit back to FintechCo) while the Marketplace private offer preserves list-price mapping for AWS settlement. That preserves a single source of truth for your finance team while not breaking marketplace reconciliation.

I'll put a worked example below (quick numbers) and loop in Jordan/Irene to confirm channel/passback mechanics for partners/resellers.

Worked example (annual committed band $1,200,000; three credit thresholds):
- Threshold A: 0–800k (no additional credit)
- Threshold B: 800k–1.2M (5% incremental usage credit on incremental tokens)
- Threshold C: 1.2M+ (10% incremental credit on incremental tokens)

Scenario: actual usage = $1,560,000 (130% of commit)
- AWS Marketplace invoice shows list-price consumption $1,560,000 routed through private offer SKU to Redwood; AWS settles to Redwood per Marketplace cadence.
- Redwood issues a post-invoice credit to FintechCo for the incremental credits: 5% on $400k (800k->1.2M) = $20k, 10% on $360k (1.2M->1.56M) = $36k; total credit $56k.
- Net economic payment by FintechCo = $1,560,000 - $56,000 = $1,504,000.

Channel/reseller effect: if you have a reseller or distributor passback, we recommend Redwood absorb the channel uplift calculation (i.e., maintain the original reseller % on list-price consumption) and apply credits net of that uplift. Practically: reseller margin is computed on the list-price settlement from AWS to Redwood; Redwood then calculates the credit that we pass back to you net of any contractual reseller fees.

I'll let Jordan/Irene confirm operational lift and whether we should push credits through AWS settlement or Redwood invoice. Internal note: Naomi, please flag any finance/recognition issues.

Next steps: Jordan/Irene — can you confirm the recommended op flow (1) Redwood issues invoice credit post-settlement or (2) send credit via AWS private-offer settlement mechanics? We'll also need to call out timing for true-ups.

Best,
David

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — tiered credits + marketplace tranche

David / team — short op recommendation from deal-ops:

Option 1 (recommended for FintechCo): Redwood issues post-invoice credits to the customer and records the AWS Marketplace settlement at list-price. Pros: clean customer GL (single vendor credit), easier for FintechCo to reconcile. Cons: Redwood takes an AP/process step to apply credits.

Option 2: Attempt to route credit through AWS private offer settlement (less common). Pros: credits appear as adjustments in marketplace settlement lines; FintechCo sees lower gross on AWS bill. Cons: requires AWS marketplace support ticketing and possible delay; reseller margin/passback can get messy because AWS may show net settlement that doesn't map cleanly to reseller proofing.

Channel margin: in both options we keep reseller % computed on AWS list-price flows. We will then compute the credit to the customer and show the net effect in the monthly reconciliation. For partners that require a proof packet, RDW will provide an itemized schedule showing list-price consumption, reseller fee, and the credit tranching.

Action items (internal):
- Naomi: confirm revenue recognition / accounting treatment for applying credits as contra-revenue vs. rebate (this affects recognition timing)
- Irene: prepare a one-page ops runbook for the FintechCo account showing invoice path, timing, settlement cadence, and supporting docs required by AWS for private-offer adjustments

Irene — can you have the runbook draft by EOD Friday? Naomi — any major red flags?

Thanks,
Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Deal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — tiered credits + marketplace tranche

Quick accounting note — prefer we treat the credits as contra-revenue (invoice credit) for this structure. Reasoning: easier to show the credit on customer statements and matches FintechCo's ask for a single vendor credit path. We should:

- Recognize revenue at gross (AWS list-price inflows) and then post the credit as contra-revenue in the period the credit is earned; ensure that deferred revenue true-ups for committed bands are handled.
- Keep clear documentation for audits: schedule that shows list-price, reseller fee, credit calculation, and net cash flow.

No showstoppers. Irene — happy to review the runbook and the example numbers once you draft.

Thanks,
Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Director, Finance — GTM, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer question — tiered credits + marketplace tranche (updated runbook and redlines)

Hi Sarah — looped in operations and finance and attached a short runbook and a redlined PO for legal. Key points we agreed internally:

- Operational flow: AWS Marketplace reports list-price consumption to Redwood. Redwood invoices per list-price and issues monthly credits to FintechCo for earned tiered credits (applied on Redwood invoice).
- Channel margin: reseller fee calculated on list-price; Redwood pays/records reseller fee per contract and credits customer net of any reseller fees where applicable.
- Timing: monthly settlement, credits applied in the following invoice cycle; true-up at quarter end if there is material variance.

I've attached: FintechCo_SOW_v1.pdf (runbook) and redlines-fintechco-20280627.docx with language clarifying 'Credits and Marketplace Settlement' (section 3.4). Please review and tell us any wording you'd prefer changed before we send to legal.

Below is a short sample invoice line item we will provide to you for transparency: 
- AWS list-price consumption: $1,560,000
- Reseller margin (15%): $234,000
- Gross to Redwood: $1,560,000 (AWS list-price settlement)
- Customer credit (tiered calc): $56,000
- Net cash due: $1,504,000

Sarah — if that aligns, we can incorporate your legal redlines and route the PO through DocuSign.

Thanks,
David
